candidates.title: Deferred domain loading for CLI startup
candidates.source: Every atlas invocation costs ~0.50 s before it does anything: ~346 ms importing atlas_agent.cli, ~75 ms building the argparse tree, ~12 ms interpreter startup. The suite spawns the CLI from 97 call sites, and the dev gate's slowest step spends 73% of its wall clock in 21 such subprocesses, so this is primarily a developer-loop cost rather than a UX one.
candidates.acceptance_criteria: A measured reduction in atlas --version wall time with the command surface unchanged: scripts/check_cli_command_compatibility.py passes, every trust-contract envelope is byte-identical, and a test pins the reduction so it cannot silently regress.
candidates.safety_notes: Import-timing and packaging only. Changes no gate, no default, and no runtime decision: not RiskManager, approval queues, kill switch, heartbeat, deadman, the audit hash-chain, live-submit opt-in, or can_submit. Loads no credentials and adds no network access. The cli_bootstrap.py pre-router keeps its four configless commands and its stdlib-only module scope.
candidates.open_question: Two levers, priced in docs/development/safety-invariant-audit-followups.md. ConfigDict(defer_build=True) measures 74% off pydantic class creation (200 synthetic models: 178 ms to 46.5 ms), about a quarter of startup, but 128 of 129 model classes inherit BaseModel directly with no shared base, and it moves a malformed model from an import-time error to a first-use error. Lazy per-domain handler import has a larger ceiling (config alone imports in 137 ms against 273 ms for cli_commands) but threads local imports through a 5.9k-line dispatch whose command surface is a pinned trust contract. Deciding which, or neither, is the candidate.

candidates.title: Wire the declared risk limits that no rule reads
candidates.source: Hard invariant 5 states RiskManager enforces limits on position size, notional, daily loss, exposure, symbols, and leverage. Four are enforced. max_daily_loss_pct is declared in RiskLimits and read by no rule, and OrderRiskInput.leverage is populated on both the paper and live-submit paths and read by no rule: a portfolio 50% down on the day against a 2% declared limit evaluates allowed=True with zero violations, as does an order carrying 10x leverage. A third limit is outside invariant 5 and worse: max_trades_per_day is configured, defaults to 5, and is one of the three lines `atlas risk check` prints to the operator, but RiskLimits has no such field and 100 trades in a day pass with zero violations. The operator is shown a limit that does not exist.
candidates.acceptance_criteria: The two xfail cases in tests/risk/test_declared_limits_are_wired.py pass with their markers removed, each new guard is verified by breaking the source and confirming the specific test fails, and no previously accepted order is rejected except by the limit being added.
candidates.safety_notes: Tightens the deterministic risk gate; enables nothing. Adds no live trading, live submit, broker or provider execution, credential loading, or network access, and changes no default toward permissiveness. It can only reject orders that are accepted today.
candidates.open_question: Resolved. Realized daily P&L is accounted at the paper broker's fill, where the position's average price is still known and where trades_today was already incremented. The config's absolute max_daily_loss and the schema's max_daily_loss_pct are different units, so both are kept as separate ceilings rather than one being folded into the other. Leverage is checked against the order, because the resolver's gate reads only the allow_leverage config flag and is satisfied when leverage is disallowed. All three limits refuse new risk only: a risk-reducing order passes every session halt, so a loss limit cannot trap a position open.

candidates.title: Map the research error codes the CLI flattens to a generic message
candidates.source: safe_research_session_error maps a ResearchSessionError to a vetted status and falls back to ('research_error', 'Research command failed.') for anything unrecognised. src/atlas_agent raises 205 distinct literal codes and RESEARCH_SESSION_ERROR_CODES maps 69 of them, so at least 136 land on the generic message. Measured over the CLI, 30 of the 175 atlas research subcommands answer a nonexistent id with 'Research command failed.' while the reason was known, static, and safe to show — for example provider_safety_dossier_source_seal_missing. A further 33 raise sites build their code at runtime and are not counted, so 136 is a lower bound.
candidates.acceptance_criteria: Entries added for the codes an operator can reach, the ratchet in tests/research/test_research_error_code_mapping.py lowered to the new count, and no status string carrying a path, identifier, or any value from the exception rather than a literal.
candidates.safety_notes: The generic fallback stays. It is the fail-safe half of this design — an unmapped exception string must never be echoed, because in general it can carry a path or user data. This only widens the vetted allowlist, so it enables nothing at runtime and changes no gate, default, or trading behaviour.
candidates.open_question: Whether all of them deserve a distinct message, or whether the families collapse into a smaller vocabulary — eleven different not-found spellings already exist across the -show commands (not_found, artifact_not_found, research_artifact_not_found, dossier_not_found, report_not_found, and more). Adding that many strings without deciding the vocabulary first would make the surface harder to consume, not easier.

candidates.title: Absorb the repeated research handler preamble
candidates.source: cli_commands/research/ holds 170 handlers over 7314 statements, median 42 statements each. 166 of them repeat the same preamble and epilogue: resolve_workspace_path(), an identical no_workspace branch printing the same JSON, a try block, `except ResearchSessionError` mapping through safe_research_session_error, and `except Exception` emitting research_error. Two handlers picked from different modules are 52% line-identical. 80 of the 170 share an AST shape with another handler.
candidates.acceptance_criteria: tests/research/test_research_command_envelopes.py passes unchanged for all 175 subcommands — same envelope, same exit status agreement — and scripts/check_cli_command_compatibility.py reports no surface change. Every handler moves, or none does: two idioms side by side would be worse than the duplication.
candidates.safety_notes: Refactor of CLI error handling and workspace resolution only. Adds no gate, removes none, and touches neither the risk gate nor the kill switch, approval queues, broker adapters, or the audit hash-chain. The fail-closed generic fallback in safe_research_session_error is preserved as-is.
candidates.open_question: Whether the shared shape is genuinely one thing or several that currently look alike. The 33 handlers that build their error code at runtime, and the four whose exit status disagrees with their envelope, are evidence the family is not as uniform as the line counts suggest. A wrapper that forces them into one shape would either paper over those differences or need escape hatches that reintroduce the duplication. Worth spiking on one module and measuring the real reduction before committing to 170.

candidates.title: L3 bounded live autonomy: explicit opt-in and the path that consults it
candidates.source: The ladder defines L3 as requiring per-order human approval, strict RiskManager limits, explicit opt-in, and active operator oversight. Three of the four now hold: approval queues exist and OrderRouter allowlists exactly manual_live; the three declared risk limits that evaluated nothing are enforced as of CAND-033; and the deadman is verified to block a hung cycle with its composition pinned. The fourth is missing — live submit has an opt-in bound to a config fingerprint, autonomy has none.
candidates.acceptance_criteria: The opt-in and the path that consults it land together: an autonomy opt-in record with its own fingerprint over the enforced limits, refused when absent, invalidated when any of those limits change, and a fail-closed L3 path that records a heartbeat. Per-order human approval is retained — a version without it is L4 and out of scope. Paper-validated before any live configuration is possible.
candidates.safety_notes: Design only at this stage; this candidate authorizes nothing. L3 is not unattended trading — per-order human approval is part of its definition. L4 remains out of reach without external legal, security, operational, risk, broker-adapter, and regulatory review by qualified parties, which the governance document requires to be done by them and not by self-assessment.
candidates.open_question: Three, recorded in the design. Whether the L3 path must record a heartbeat explicitly, since an absent heartbeat reads as fresh and the deadman is inert on any path that evaluates without recording. What 'active operator oversight' means as a signal — a deadman proves the agent is alive, not that a human is watching. And how narrow the first cut should be; the ladder says tightly bounded, and one symbol, one side, one broker, paper-validated first is what makes the review worth doing.

candidates.title: Absorb the per-artifact helper copies verified identical
candidates.source: src/atlas_agent/research/ holds ~30 modules, one per artifact type, each written by copying its predecessor. Comparing the unparsed source of every module-level function finds 83 definitions byte-identical to another module's: _check_name x24, validate_provider_id x21, validate_model_id x20, _get_disabled_provider_ids x16, _is_inside_workspace x9, _has_unsafe_positive_claims x9, _build_broker_separation_policy x8. Eight of the nine families had not drifted; the ninth had, and it was the one whose copies were not byte-identical.
candidates.acceptance_criteria: Scoped to the helper families whose copies are byte-identical and verified identical on substance including transitive dependencies: _check_name, validate_model_id, _get_disabled_provider_ids, _is_inside_workspace, _build_broker_separation_policy, _has_unsafe_positive_claims. Each family collapsed to one definition, the per-artifact error code kept as an argument, a structural test preventing regrowth, and the research suite passing unchanged.
candidates.safety_notes: Validator and artifact-loader plumbing. No gate added or removed, and no change to the risk gate, kill switch, approval queues, broker adapters, or the audit hash-chain. The one behavioural change is the unsafe-claim vocabulary, which only refuses more.
candidates.open_question: Resolved for this scope: 76 copies collapsed across six families. validate_provider_id is excluded by scope, not left undone -- normalising its error code away leaves three disjoint admission rules under one name (15 copies accept the four disabled external provider ids and reject mock, 5 accept only mock, 1 accepts both), so unifying it is a policy change rather than a dedup. It carries forward as CAND-038. The larger structure-only clusters were re-measured and are not a mechanical lever: only 4 of ~24 lines are identical across all 12 validate_*_artifact copies, so the earlier 2,208-line estimate measured shape rather than content.
